title: Hearthstone KYC automation pilot notes
content:
Call notes (2025-11-03) - Hearthstone Mortgage - initial scoping call
Attendees: Samira (Head of Ops), Ben (CTO), Tasha (Ops), Riley (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Anya (Solutions PM)

High level ask
- Automate KYC / ID verification + basic income proof extraction from customer-submitted docs for mortgage origination.
- Reduce manual review volume by ~60% on first pass.
- Keep final manual signoff for edge cases.

Customer pain points / context
- Current process: agents manually review PDFs, photos uploaded via web/app; high seasonal spikes (30k doc uploads/month peak).
- Main doc types: driver license, passport, utility bills, bank statements, signed application PDFs. Many multi-page PDFs with embedded scans.
- Quality issues: variable lighting, rotated pages, compression artifacts, signed forms with scribbles that break OCR.
- Regulations: must retain chain-of-custody, redaction of SSNs before downstream analytics; audit trail for all extracted fields.
- Data residency: production needs to run in their VPC (private deployment) in us-east-1, HSM/KMS integration required.

Non-functional constraints / targets discussed
- Throughput target: baseline 10k documents/day, peak spikes up to 30k/day.
- Latency: batch-friendly but want per-document metadata extraction under ~4s (median) and full structured extraction pipeline within 15s for interactive review flow.
- Accuracy: target 98% field-level accuracy for name/DOB/ID-number on good-quality images; degrade gracefully and surface confidence.
- Security: end-to-end TLS, no model weights/extracted PII to leave customer's VPC; logs kept in customer-controlled bucket with retention policy.

Preferred deployment
- Customer preference: Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem package for regulated data. They asked about Dedicated as a fallback for non-PII workloads.
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with AWS KMS + optional HSM for signing audit logs.

Initial technical approach (rough)
- Ingest connector: S3 events -> Redwood Private API (signed) or direct SFTP drop (TBD).
- Preprocessing: image normalization, rotation detection, PDF unpacking, page-level OCR (Tesseract or commercial OCR) -> produce text + position metadata.
- Two-stage extraction: rule-based heuristics + LLM model for noisy cases (layout + context aware extraction). LLM used only on sanitized inputs (PII redaction step optional per policy).
- Confidence scoring: numeric per-field confidence and provenance (OCR confidence + model token-level scores).
- Human-in-loop: create reviewer queue for low-confidence docs via customer UI (they use an internal queueing tool; integration via webhook).
- Auditing: store raw inputs (encrypted), extracted JSON, transformation logs, and model decision traces for compliance.

Data & evals
- They will provide a sample of ~1,000 labeled pages (redacted) for initial evals. Need schema mapping doc.
- Ask: want example golden set format (CSV/JSONL) and instructions for labeling.
- Concern: many fields are in different formats across states (ID formats differ) -> need canonicalizers per-state.

Gotchas / risks called out on the call
- OCR + LLM hallucination: must avoid hallucinated ID numbers; prefer to surface as low-confidence and defer to human.
- Multi-language: some applicants non-English (Spanish commonly). Need language detection and fallback.
- Signed PDFs with flattened images: extraction harder; may require page-level segmentation heuristics.
- Encrypted / password-protected PDFs: need defined behavior (reject + notify).
- Large attachments (100+MB) — define max size and async handling.
- Retention/erase requests: must provide straightforward deletion of raw files + derived artifacts with audit.

Acceptance criteria for pilot MVP (agreed loosely)
- End-to-end pipeline in customer's VPC processing sample dataset (1k pages) with logs accessible.
- Field extraction accuracy >= 95% on provided golden set for core fields (name, DOB, ID#).
- Reviewer queue integration + sample dashboard showing throughput and false-positive rates.
- Documented onboarding & runbook for incidents.

Proposed scope for initial POC (4 weeks)
- Week 0: kickoff, access provisioning (VPC peering, test S3 bucket, KMS test keys).
- Week 1: ingest + OCR pipeline + basic extraction heuristics; demo unstructured -> simple JSON.
- Week 2: LLM extraction model integration for noisy docs; confidence scoring; UI hooks for reviewer queue.
- Week 3: metrics + audit logs; run golden set; adjust heuristics; prepare handoff doc + runbook.

Open questions (need answers before SOW)
- Can Hearthstone provide a non-production S3 with representative filenames and a sample golden set by 2025-11-14?
- Do they require FIPS-compliant KMS/HSM for pilot or only for production?
- What is the exact retention window for raw images (30/90/365 days)?
- Are there internal SLAs for reviewer turnaround we must accommodate?

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Riley: send short architecture sketch + list of infra access we need (by 2025-11-05).
- Marco: prepare golden-set template + labeling guidance (by 2025-11-07).
- Samira: share sample S3 + 1k redacted pages or give access (by 2025-11-14).
- Anya: draft SOW + high-level cost estimate for 8-week pilot (by 2025-11-11).
- Liam: scope KMS/HSM compliance checklist and any additional legal redlines to flag (by 2025-11-10).

Notes to self / conversation fragments (raw)
- Samira: "we cannot have candidate SSNs persist in any external logs" -> emphasize deletion + encryption at rest.
- Ben: "ideally we get under 15s per doc for interactive review" -> edge-case performance.
- Tasha: wants reviewer UI to show one-click escalate to manual underwriting.
- Potential friction: Legal may require entire pipeline in-customer VPC (we should price accordingly).

Things to prototype quickly
- Small lambda to unzip PDFs, OCR, produce JSONL + confidence fields. Hook to Redwood dev instance for testing.
- Quick eval harness: compare OCR-only vs OCR+LLM extraction on 200 pages to spot hallucination patterns.

File TODOs (housekeeping)
- Add sample form mapping for driver licenses (state list).
- Add language detection fallback block to extraction pipeline.
- Create demo script for 10-min internal demo showing error cases.

Bottom line (short)
- Customer motivated, regulatory constraints push private deployment. Pilot looks feasible in 4–8 weeks with a small SE + solutions effort. Key dependencies: sample data, KMS access decision, retention policy.
summary: Scratchpad for Hearthstone Mortgage KYC automation pilot — call notes, constraints, pilot scope, technical approach, risks, and immediate next steps.
